newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX Euroyen steady after Fed inspires new high.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX Euroyen steady after Fed inspires new high.

text.p: SIMEX Euroyen futures ended little changed on Wednesday after reaching a new overnight high in Chicago following the Federal Reserve's decision to leave short-term U.S. interest rates unchanged.
"There were stops going off in Euroyen as we went above the previous high. But the volume has been decidedly light," said Mark Falconer, sales desk manager at NatWest Futures.
March Euroyen ended at 99.21 against its CME close and new contract high of 99.23. Turnover was an estimated 7,125 lots.
Japanese government bond (JGB) futures for December settled at 122.23 against their opening 122.25.

Dealers said there was no obvious explanation for the Japanese yield curve's rally on the back of the Fed decision, except that it reinforced the view that the Bank of Japan would have even less reason to hike rates.

"You can't afford not to be bullish on Euroyen and JGBs. Every time we have some bad news, the market just pulls back five ticks because there are people queuing up to buy at the low end," Falconer said.

He said March Euroyen would find good buying interest near 99.18, but its upside looked toppish. "There's a real risk rates will be moved higher before the March expiry," he said, adding that the contract's target of 99.33 looked excessive.
December Eurodollars finished at 94.16 against their IMM settlement at 94.18.
